description: Statically derived by reading app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, never captured from a run: the COBOL cannot be executed in this environment - there is no z/OS and no CICS emulator, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - so every value below is read out of the source, the copybooks, the symbolic map and the fixture rather than recorded from an execution. This is the folder's NOT-Y-OR-N rejection - paragraph 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS at :845-874 - and what it pins beyond the rejection itself is that THE CHECK IS CASE SENSITIVE: a user who types a lower-case 'y' into the active-status field is refused by a program whose own stored data holds nothing but 'Y'. The construction has to be stated before the trace, because reaching 1240 at all takes more than an invalid status. Row 1 of fixtures/carddata.txt is seeded and snapshotted, so CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME is the upper-cased 'ANIYA VON' that case06.json derived, CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR/EXPMON/EXPDAY are '2023'/'03'/'09' and CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD is 'Y'. The resubmitted CRDSTCDI is 'y', which is a DELIBERATELY INVALID INPUT AND NOT FIXTURE DATA: an exhaustive scan of all fifty rows shows CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS is the single character 'Y' in every one of them, so no stored record could ever supply the lower-case form and no amount of seeding would produce it - the operator's keyboard is the only source, which is precisely the path this case tests. CRDNAMEI and EXPYEARI are resubmitted UNCHANGED from the snapshot so that 1230 and 1260 take their success limbs, and EXPMONI is resubmitted as '07' rather than the snapshot '03' for a reason set out in full below. '07' is itself grounded in the shipped data rather than invented: six of the fifty fixture rows carry expiry month 07, among them row 2, card 0683586198171516, account 00000000027, CVV 567, name 'Ward Jones', expiry 2025-07-13 - so the month submitted here is a value the legacy file genuinely stores, and it is valid under this program's own edit. EIBCALEN is 489, which is 160 + 329 - the width COMMON-RETURN hands back at :549-557, where 160 is CARDDEMO-COMMAREA summed mechanically from app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 and 329 is WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :274-321 as 1 (CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION) + 89 (CCUP-OLD-DETAILS: 11 + 16 + 3 + 59) + 89 (CCUP-NEW-DETAILS) + 150 (CARD-UPDATE-RECORD: 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59). So the :388 guard fails EQUAL TO 0, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LIT-CCLISTPGM ('COCRDLIC', :227-228) rather than LIT-MENUPGM, and the ELSE at :396-400 restores CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(1:160) and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(161:329), so the inbound ids and the whole CCUP-OLD-* snapshot SURVIVE. The case contract keys a commarea value by the copybook name and admits the CDEMO- items of the shared area plus the WS- items of the receiving program's own extension; COCRDUPC names its extension items CCUP-*, which neither form covers, so the extension is declared under the one legal name the source itself gives the whole span, WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, carrying the exact 329-byte image that single MOVE restores. Its bytes decode as CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION [1] 'S' (88 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :281), then CCUP-OLD-DETAILS [2-90] as CCUP-OLD-ACCTID [2-12] '00000000050', CCUP-OLD-CARDID [13-28] '0500024453765740', CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD [29-31] '747', CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME [32-81] 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50, CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR [82-85] '2023', CCUP-OLD-EXPMON [86-87] '03', CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY [88-89] '09' and CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD [90] 'Y' - the snapshot exactly as case06.json derived it, with the INSPECT CONVERTING fold at :1356-1358 already applied and the three reference-modified slices (1:4)/(6:2)/(9:2) of the ten-byte 'YYYY-MM-DD' already taken - then CCUP-NEW-DETAILS [91-179] and CARD-UPDATE-RECORD [180-329] as spaces, which is what the :586 INITIALIZE and the :1461 INITIALIZE respectively leave in a PIC X group. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 (REENTER) and ENTER is admitted unchanged by :413-424, because :414 lists CCARD-AID-ENTER among the four combinations it accepts. The ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :429 is then gate G30 read downwards: arm one (:435-439) needs PF03 or a done/failed state with CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET equal to LIT-CCLISTMAPSET, and the AID is ENTER with the state 'S'; arm two (:482-485) needs CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, which REENTER denies, or CCARD-AID-PFK12, which ENTER denies; arm three (:502-505) needs CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED with CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, or an arrival from LIT-MENUPGM; arm four (:517-518) needs 'C', 'L' or 'F'. So WHEN OTHER at :535 performs 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION and 3000-SEND-MAP as range performs and leaves through GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :542. Reaching 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS is also why this case names a next program: :570-572 move LIT-THISPGM, LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP into CCARD-NEXT-PROG, CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP, so the response carries 'COCRDUPC' as well as the mapset and map - case06.json, which reaches 3000-SEND-MAP through arm two instead, carries no next program at all. 1100-RECEIVE-MAP :578-636 INITIALIZEs CCUP-NEW-DETAILS at :586 and then normalises each field, mapping '*' or SPACES to LOW-VALUES; CRDSTCDI is neither, so :614-619 takes the ELSE limb at :617-618 and moves 'y' VERBATIM into CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD - there is no fold, no trim and no coercion on this path. Two source oddities are preserved rather than tidied. MOVE EXPDAYI OF CCRDUPAI TO CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY at :621 is UNCONDITIONAL - alone among the six data moves it carries no '*'/SPACES guard - and it is left that way. And CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD is never assigned anywhere in the program, because the COCRDUP map has no CVV field, so it keeps the SPACES the :586 INITIALIZE gave it; this case declines to hide that rather than pinning it, since nothing is written here for it to corrupt. 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS :641-715 SETs INPUT-OK at :643 and then finds IF CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED false, so it takes the ELSE CONTINUE at :663-664: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT and 1220-EDIT-CARD are NOT performed, and neither is the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA at :653 that would have wiped the fifty-nine bytes just received. Execution continues past :667 with SET FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT (:668), SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID and SET FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID (:669-670), and then :671-677 copy the snapshot outwards into CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS and the three REDEFINES sub-fields CARD-EXPIRY-DAY, CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH and CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR declared at :115-123 over CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X PIC X(10) (4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10), which is gate G34. THE DETECTOR AT :680-683 IS THE TRAP THIS CASE HAD TO BE BUILT AROUND, AND IT IS WORTH THE ARITHMETIC. IF (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) EQUAL FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA)) compares the whole GROUP and not field by field; from :295-301 and :307-313 each group is CRDNAME X(50) + EXPIRAION-DATE (EXPYEAR X(4) + EXPMON X(2) + EXPDAY X(2)) + CRDSTCD X(1), summing mechanically to 50 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 59 bytes, so within the group CRDNAME occupies [1-50], EXPYEAR [51-54], EXPMON [55-56], EXPDAY [57-58] and CRDSTCD [59]. BOTH OPERANDS ARE FOLDED TO UPPER CASE. Had the status been the only thing resubmitted differently, the fold would have turned 'y' back into 'Y', the two 59-byte groups would have compared EQUAL, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED would have been set at :682 and the three-way IF at :685-687 would have forced all four flags ISVALID and taken the GO TO at :692 - 1240 WOULD NEVER HAVE RUN, and the case would have silently become a duplicate of case09.json while still looking like a status test. That is the whole reason EXPMONI is '07': worked byte by byte, UPPER-CASE(OLD) is 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50, then '2023', '03', '09', 'Y' and UPPER-CASE(NEW) is the same 50 bytes, then '2023', '07', '09', 'Y', so the two differ at EXACTLY ONE POSITION, group byte 56, the second digit of the month - a difference in DIGITS, which no case fold can erase. The comparison therefore fails, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is NOT set, and the observable consequence is asserted as an absence: the 88 at :187-188, 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.', appears NOWHERE in this expectation. The first limb of :685-687 being false, and the state being 'S' rather than 'N' or 'C', the skip does not fire and execution reaches SET CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :696, so THE STATE BECOMES 'E' BEFORE A SINGLE EDIT EXECUTES. That ordering is not incidental - it is what arms the CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK guard on every data-field highlight below, and a translation that set the state after the edits, or only on failure, would paint an unhighlighted screen and still pass most of this folder. The four edits then run in source order at :698-708, and only the second of them fails. 1230-EDIT-NAME :806-840 SUCCEEDS: the blank test at :811-813 fails because the name is populated, :823 moves it into CARD-NAME-CHECK PIC X(50), :824-826 INSPECTs it CONVERTING LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM ('ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz', :255-257) TO LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO (SPACES, :258-259), and because 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50 holds nothing but letters and spaces every letter blanks out and the result is fifty spaces, so IF FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(CARD-NAME-CHECK)) = 0 at :828 takes the CONTINUE at :829 and :839 SETs FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID - the '1' asserted here. No message is written, and that matters: the alphabetic-only text of :183-184 belongs to case10.json, which submits the one stored name in the whole fixture that contains a non-letter. THE HEADLINE IS 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS :845-874. SET FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :847 leaves the flag at '0' before anything is tested. The blank test at :850-852 - IF CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES OR EQUAL ZEROS - FAILS, because 'y' is populated; that branch, and the FLG-CARDSTATUS-BLANK it sets at :854, belong to case14.json and not here. :861 then moves CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD into FLG-YES-NO-CHECK, declared at :89-91 as PIC X(1) VALUE 'N' with 88 FLG-YES-NO-VALID VALUES 'Y', 'N' - TWO UPPER-CASE LITERALS AND NOTHING ELSE. An 88 is a byte comparison against the literals as written, so 'y' (x'79' in ASCII) matches neither, IF FLG-YES-NO-VALID at :863 is FALSE, the ISVALID limb at :864 is not taken, and the ELSE at :865-871 runs: SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE at :866, SET FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :867 which merely holds the flag at the '0' :847 already wrote, then, GUARDED BY IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :868, SET CARD-STATUS-MUST-BE-YES-NO TO TRUE - the 88 at :195-196, 'Card Active Status must be Y or N' - and GO TO 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS-EXIT at :871. The guard ADMITS the message because :384 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF cleared WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) on entry and nothing between there and here has written it: this is the FIRST error on the path, which is exactly why the three sibling edits were deliberately given valid inputs. THE CASE SENSITIVITY IS THE FINDING AND IT IS PRESERVED, NOT CORRECTED. Nothing in this program upper-cases the status field on the way in: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP moves it verbatim at :618, and the only two INSPECT ... CONVERTING LIT-LOWER TO LIT-UPPER statements in the whole program, at :1356-1358 in 9000-READ-DATA and at :1499-1501 in 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC, both operate on CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME and on nothing else. So the legacy screen refuses a lower-case 'y' while accepting 'Y', and a translation that folded the status - one plausible line of tidying - would accept an input the mainframe rejects and would be a changed business rule. THE TWO BRANCHES OF THIS PARAGRAPH SHARE ONE MESSAGE, which is why the flag is asserted and not just the text. :856 (blank) and :869 (invalid) both SET CARD-STATUS-MUST-BE-YES-NO, so ERRMSGO alone cannot tell the two apart; only WS-EDIT-CARDSTATUS-FLAG can, and its 88s at :69-72 give FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK '0' here against FLG-CARDSTATUS-BLANK ' ' in the blank branch. The '0' is what separates this case from case14.json, and it is observable at one remove through the cursor and the highlight derived below, both of which key off FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK specifically. 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON and 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR then both SUCCEED: CCUP-NEW-EXPMON '07' moves to CARD-MONTH-CHECK at :896 and its numeric REDEFINES view satisfies 88 VALID-MONTH VALUES 1 THRU 12 at :92-95, so :898-899 sets FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID; CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR '2023' moves to CARD-YEAR-CHECK at :932 and satisfies 88 VALID-YEAR VALUES 1950 THRU 2099 at :96-99, so :934-935 sets FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-ISVALID. Their IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guards at :903 and :939 would have suppressed a second message even had one of them failed, but this case does not lean on that: the inputs are genuinely valid and all three sibling flags are genuinely '1', which is what makes the single highlight and the single cursor position below unambiguous. At :710-714 IF INPUT-ERROR CONTINUE ELSE SET CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, and INPUT-ERROR was set inside 1240, so 'N' is not set and the state remains 'E'. 2000-DECIDE-ACTION :948-1027 is read in source order too: arm (a) WHEN CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :954 fails, arm (b) WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 at :958 fails because ENTER was pressed, arm (c) WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :971 fails because the state is no longer 'S', and arm (d) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :982-983 matches and CONTINUEs (gate G30, the arm chosen by source order). That single CONTINUE is what prevents any write attempt, because 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING is reachable only from the :988-989 arm requiring CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED together with PF05: no repository call of any kind occurs on this path, not a read, not a read-for-update and not a rewrite, and 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC is never entered either. 3000-SEND-MAP :1035-1045 then runs 3100, 3200, 3250, 3300 and 3400 in that order, and that order is load-bearing for the cursor derivation below. 3100 fills CCRDUPAO with LOW-VALUES at :1053 - which is why every colour item starts at x'00', the byte DFHBMSCA names DFHDFCOL - and moves the two active COTTL01Y titles (line 21 of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy is commented out in column 7, so TITLE02O is the active line 22) together with LIT-THISTRANID, LIT-THISPGM and the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings of the pinned clock. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS :1082-1134 runs its ELSE limb because the context is REENTER; CC-ACCT-ID-N and CC-CARD-NUM-N are both non-zero from the :591-604 loads, so ACCTSIDO carries '00000000050' at X(11) and CARDSIDO '0500024453765740' at X(16); and the inner four-arm ordered EVALUATE at :1099 passes over arm one (:1100 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, false) and arm two (:1107 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS, false now that the state is 'E') to match arm three at :1113, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-MADE - the grouping 88 at :282-284 whose values are 'E', 'N', 'C', 'L' and 'F'. Its body at :1114-1123 paints the CCUP-NEW-* values, so THE OFFENDING INPUT IS ECHOED BACK: CRDSTCDO is the lower-case 'y' the user typed and not the stored 'Y'. Two fields make that arm choice VALUE-DISTINGUISHABLE rather than merely structural, and the changed month is the second of them: EXPMONO is '07' where the OLD snapshot holds '03', so an implementation that had painted CCUP-OLD-* instead - arm two's body, or the WHEN OTHER at :1124-1129 - would differ observably in two independent fields. That is the exact contrast with case09.json, where the skip left the state at 'S', arm two matched, and the user's typing was DISCARDED in favour of the stored value: one EVALUATE, two arms, opposite treatments of the same screen fields. The day is the exception and is preserved as written: :1122 is a COMMENTED-OUT MOVE CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and :1123 moves CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY instead, under a source comment explaining that the field is not one the user is allowed to change, so EXPDAYO is taken from the OLD snapshot. Honesty about the strength of that assertion matters more than the appearance of one: EXPDAYI is resubmitted as the '09' that 3200 painted and :1285 renders dark, so CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY coincide here and the choice at :1123 is preserved structurally but is NOT distinguishable by value on this path - stated rather than overclaimed, exactly as the unconditional :621 is. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG :1138-1163 is ordered the same way: arm one :1141 CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is false, arm two :1143 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is false, arm three :1145 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS is false, and arm four :1147-1148 WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK matches, so SET PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES puts the 88 literal of :164-165 into WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) and :1161 paints INFOMSGO as 'Update card details presented above.' - the trailing full stop is INSIDE the literal - with four trailing spaces to reach X(40). :1163 then moves WS-RETURN-MSG into the X(80) ERRMSGO, so the thirty-three characters of 'Card Active Status must be Y or N' are followed by forty-seven spaces. Neither CSMSG01Y literal appears: the thank-you and invalid-key texts have zero references anywhere in this program. GATE G38, THE CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK-GUARDED HALF, IS THE REASON THIS CASE CARRIES A COLOUR MAP AT ALL. COCRDUPC does not COPY CSSETATY; it re-implements the error highlight inline at :1243-1307, AND THE GUARD IS NOT THE SAME FOR EVERY FIELD GROUP. The two search keys are guarded by AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :1247 and :1257, and their flags were set ISVALID at :669-670, so neither the '*' nor the DFHRED fires for them here - that half of the gate is proved by case03.json, where 1210 and 1220 do run and both keys redden. The four data fields are guarded by AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK instead, and this case is where that guard is satisfied for the status: IF FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :1274-1277 has a '0' flag from :847 and :867 and an 'E' state from :696, so MOVE DFHRED TO CRDSTCDC FIRES and CRDSTCDC is the one colour item that differs from DFHDFCOL by an error. Its '*' companion at :1279-1283 requires FLG-CARDSTATUS-BLANK and does NOT fire, which is why CRDSTCDO keeps the echoed 'y' rather than being overwritten with an asterisk - the two guards are five lines apart, they share a message, and a translation that confused them would blank the very field the user must correct and would also lose the evidence of which branch ran. CRDNAMEC, EXPMONC and EXPYEARC take no DFHRED, because :1263-1272, :1287-1296 and :1298-1307 all test flags that 1230, 1250 and 1260 set ISVALID. EXPDAYC carries DFHBMDAR from the unconditional MOVE at :1285. Two further attribute writes land on xxxA items, which are the attribute REDEFINES of the xxxF flag bytes rather than the xxxC colour items this contract admits, so they are recorded here in the audit trail instead: :1309-1313 moves DFHBMBRY to INFOMSGA because WS-INFO-MSG is not blank, and :1315-1317 leaves FKEYSCA alone because PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is false. Colours are named by their common/BmsAttributes mnemonics throughout rather than by raw bytes, so a failing comparison reports 'DFHRED' and not 0xF2. The :1238-1241 arm is nonetheless taken, since CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is the 'COCRDLI' the card list left there, and it moves DFHDFCOL to ACCTSIDC and CARDSIDC - which is the x'00' that :1053 had already written, a genuine branch with no observable effect, and saying so is cheaper than wondering later. 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS' protection matrix at :1172-1207 matches the arm group at :1181-1190, WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS / WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, because 'E' satisfies the second: DFHBMPRF goes to ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA, the two search keys now protected, and DFHBMFSE to CRDNAMEA, CRDSTCDA, EXPMONA and EXPYEARA, the four fields the user may still edit, with EXPDAYA commented out at :1185. Those five also land on xxxA items and are likewise recorded here rather than in the attributes member. The cursor EVALUATE at :1211-1235 is ordered and moves -1 exactly once, and the derivation has one trap in it. FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT at :1212 is an 88 on WS-INFO-MSG, and although :668 did set it, 3250 has since OVERWRITTEN WS-INFO-MSG with PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES - 3250 runs before 3300 per the call order at :1036-1045 - so the first arm group no longer matches; NO-CHANGES-DETECTED at :1213 is an 88 on WS-RETURN-MSG, which now holds the status text, so it fails too; the account arms at :1215-1216 and the card arms at :1218-1219 fail on the ISVALID filters; the name arms at :1221-1222 fail because 1230 set FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID; and the FIRST MATCH is WHEN FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK at :1224, which moves -1 into CRDSTCDL at :1226. The cursor therefore rests on the field the message is about, and it rests there BECAUSE the flag is '0' - the same fact ERRMSGO cannot express. xxxL is metadata expressed as the cursor and never as a payload member. Every payload width is the xxxI item's own from app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY (4/40/8/8/40/8/11/16/50/1/2/4/2/40/80/21/18), and FKEYSO and FKEYSCO stay at LOW-VALUES because the program never writes them - their text is a physical-map INITIAL in app/bms/COCRDUP.bms that CICS merges at send time. Gate G37: the whole conversation state travels in the payload - the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 329-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA that :549-557 concatenates - and none of it is held server-side, so CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT comes back as 1, CDEMO-ACCT-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM come back unchanged because :671-672 rewrote them from a snapshot holding the identical values, CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION comes back as 'E' rather than the 'S' it arrived as, and the transaction ends on the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(LIT-THISTRANID) of COMMON-RETURN at :554-558. Nothing is written: validation failed, so 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING is never entered, and expectedWrites is empty as a POSITIVE assertion that no write occurred rather than as an omission - CARDDAT is additionally declared with zero rows on the WRITES channel to say exactly that. The final state pins the other half of it: all three seeded rows byte-identical to the seed, with row 1's CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME still the mixed-case 'Aniya Von' it was seeded with and its CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS still 'Y', which proves that the rejected 'y' reached no dataset and that the fold at :1356-1358 is contained to the in-memory copy - 9000-READ-DATA is not performed on this arm at all, so the fold never even runs. The seed is genuine fixture data - rows 1 to 3 of fixtures/carddata.txt, byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - and row 1 decodes at the CVACT02Y offsets as CARD-NUM [1-16] '0500024453765740', CARD-ACCT-ID [17-27] '00000000050', CARD-CVV-CD [28-30] '747', CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME [31-80] 'Aniya Von' padded to 50, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE [81-90] '2023-03-09' - the copybook's own misspelling, preserved verbatim, because renaming it would break field-for-field diffing - CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS [91] 'Y' and FILLER [92-150] fifty-nine spaces, the widths summing mechanically to 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59 = 150 (gate G19), and the FILLER is pinned rather than omitted because a codec that dropped it would shorten every record and shift every later offset. No normalisation is declared because carddata.txt already ships at its full copybook width; only cardxref.txt needs the pad. The clock is pinned to this source's own version footer so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are assertable at all, the charset is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to the platform default, and the return code is 0 because COCRDUPC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' - gate G35 has nothing to bind to here, just as G32 has nothing (this program's GO TOs are all forward, the :871 one included) and G39 has nothing (this screen does not paginate). This is case 11 of the twenty this program owns (gate G15), it is judged by field-for-field diffing to a count of zero (gate G18), and the unit is reached as a plain object - no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided.', so no user rule governs this fixture and none has been invented; it is held instead to the enterprise practices the migration adopts in their place - B1 (every value verified against source, copybook or fixture, no placeholder), B3 (the COBOL, the copybooks, the map and app/data are read and never written), B4 (the case14.json overlap and the non-distinguishable :1123 are documented rather than papered over), B5 (the unconditional :621, the never-assigned CVV, the commented-out :1122 and the case-sensitive 88 all preserved as written), B7 (deterministic: pinned clock, fixed seed, no wall-clock and no random), B8 (explicit widths, explicit trailing spaces, explicit charset), B9 (self-contained, no shared mutable state), B11 (the 59-byte group and the 150-byte record summed by hand and shown) and B12 (the impossibility of a captured baseline stated up front rather than absorbed).

fields.ERRMSGO: Card Active Status must be Y or N
